content:
I have to admit, my DIY iPhone camera mod looks pretty ridiculous — but it actually makes shooting photos and videos on the iPhone more practical and more enjoyable.

Originally it was meant to solve a specific video-shooting scenario, but unexpectedly, I found myself reaching for it again and again…

In the world of compact cameras, one of the longest-running debates is whether you need a viewfinder. Enthusiasts have long argued for electronic viewfinders (EVF) over optical ones, but EVFs are now so good that basically nobody minds the difference anymore.

But whether optical or electronic, a viewfinder offers a very practical advantage over framing with the rear screen, especially in bright sunlight. Even with the screen brightness turned all the way up, when the sun is harsh, it can still be very hard to see what you're shooting, and you may also have to deal with screen glare.

Although London hasn't traditionally been a big problem, this summer brought a record-breaking heatwave, and honestly, I think the last time I saw it rain was about thirty years ago.

But to me, it's about more than that. I feel there's a psychological difference between only seeing what's inside the frame and seeing the surrounding environment while taking the shot. Sometimes it's precisely this that makes me prefer to use a dedicated camera instead of a phone.

When I was choosing a video camera a few years ago, the Blackmagic Pocket Cinema Camera 4K was the obvious popular choice, but the lack of a viewfinder put me off. In the end I decided it wasn't a big deal for me, because I mostly use it indoors, and when I go outside, attaching a large monitor with a sun hood solves most of the issues.

But sometimes I want something more lightweight than a full rig with an external monitor, so I found a simple accessory for outdoor use. It's a combo sun hood and loupe that magnetically attaches to the camera's rear screen, effectively giving you an optical viewfinder.

I had an upcoming shoot where I needed to shoot with both the BMPCC 4K and an iPhone 16 Pro Max. I did a quick test on location and found the viewfinder accessory really useful. Since the screen size on the BMPCC 4K is close to the iPhone's, I wondered if I could use it on the iPhone as well.

Of course the iPhone has no magnetic mounting, but the iPhone is light enough that holding it up against the loupe works perfectly fine. The results blew me away, especially when using the Camera Control button as a shutter.

Since then, I've used this accessory in quite a few shooting situations, and both being able to see the screen more clearly in harsh sunlight and that feeling of immersion make the whole experience more enjoyable. My iPhone has long been my go-to camera, and with this DIY mod, I think there will be even more situations where just bringing my phone is enough.

Is this design ridiculous or genius? Let me know what you think in the comments. If you think it's the latter, sorry to say, but the product I bought seems to have been discontinued, and I haven't seen a similar design made for screens over three inches. If you find one, please drop a link in the comments.
